key_insight: The paper shows that the finite-size Dicke model can be simulated with variational quantum algorithms on both qubit-only and hybrid qubit-boson hardware while preserving the model’s critical collective light-matter behavior.
engineering_relevance: It provides a scalable, symmetry-aware route for near-term quantum devices to study spin-boson and light-matter systems with fewer resources than fully general-purpose simulations.
method: Built a variational framework for the finite-size Dicke model on digital qubit platforms.
Developed a hybrid digital-analogue qubit-boson ansatz that directly uses bosonic degrees of freedom.
Benchmarked behavior in classical emulators and on trapped-ion quantum hardware.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the approach reproduces Dicke-model critical behavior in the large-spin limit and is implementable on both emulators and trapped-ion devices.
watch_item: Performance on current trapped-ion hardware is limited by noise, which may constrain accuracy and scalability.
paper_title: Simulating the Dicke Model on Qubit-Based and hybrid Qubit-Boson-Based Quantum Computers
